title: Same Judgment, Different Yes: Measuring Multilingual Judgment Profiles in Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring answer habits including yes/no keying bias, second-listed preference (order bias), and named-term pull (acquiescence bias) by systematically varying question forms (e.g., plain polar, negative interrogatives, alternative questions), evaluative wordings, and answer constraints (e.g., forced yes/no tokens vs. free sentences) on moral vignettes.

Evaluating and comparing model responses across six languages (English, Chinese, German, Japanese, Korean, French) to isolate variations caused by language-specific grammatical and answering conventions (such as how a language maps 'yes' or 'no' to negative interrogatives) from genuine shifts in the model's underlying judgment profile.
